model ModBuild {
  id            String    @id @default(cuid())
  userId        String
  /// queued | planning | coding | compiling | repairing | scanning | succeeded | failed
  status        String    @default("queued")
  prompt        String
  /// Set for an iteration ("Ask for a change"): what the user asked to change.
  changeRequest String?
  /// The build this one iterates on (same user).
  baseBuildId   String?
  /// The first build of this plugin's history (self for a fresh build).
  rootBuildId   String?
  mcVersion     String
  pluginName    String?
  version       String?
  /// Mirror of the service's result: summary, commands, permissions, config,
  /// warnings, files, safety, events. Shape: lib/modbuilder/types.ts ModBuildResult.
  result        Json?
  error         String?
  errorCode     String?
  attempts      Int       @default(0)
  /// AI spend as reported by the service (USD, API-equivalent).
  costUsd       Float     @default(0)
  durationMs    Int?
  jarName       String?
  jarSize       Int?
  jarSha256     String?
  /// Absolute path of the stored jar on the primary.
  jarPath       String?
  /// Last install to a server: { serverId, serverName, at, backup?, restarted }.
  lastInstall   Json?
  /// Cyrus (2026-10-07, additive): per-build { model, attachments[] } and, on a
  /// project's ROOT build, per-project { title, favourite, notes, headBuildId }.
  /// Shape: lib/cyrus/meta.ts CyrusMeta. Null for builds made in the old UI.
  cyrus         Json?
  createdAt     DateTime  @default(now())
  updatedAt     DateTime  @updatedAt
  finishedAt    DateTime?

  @@index([userId, createdAt])
  @@index([status])
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Cyrus token economy (2026-10-07, branch feature/cyrus-tokens). ADDITIVE ONLY.
// lib/cyrus/tokens/* is the only writer. Design + numbers:
// docs/DOCUMENTATION.md "Cyrus token economy" and /root/agent-notes/cyrus-economy/ECONOMY.md.
// No relations to User on purpose (same convention as ModBuild): rows are keyed by userId.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// One row per account that ever held Cyrus tokens. Locked FOR UPDATE by every
/// ledger operation, so all of one account's token writes are serialised.
/// `balance` and `reserved` are caches: the truth is SUM(CyrusTokenLot.remaining)
/// over unexpired lots, and SUM(CyrusTokenReservation.amount) over held holds.
model CyrusTokenAccount {
  userId          String    @id
  balance         Int       @default(0)
  reserved        Int       @default(0)
model CyrusModPage {
  id            String    @id @default(cuid())
  /// ModBuild.rootBuildId shared by every version of this mod.
  rootBuildId   String    @unique
  /// The creator (ModBuild.userId).
  userId        String
  /// Public URL slug: /mods/cyrus/<slug>, /dashboard/nxlabs/cyrus/<slug>.
  slug          String    @unique
  title         String
  tagline       String?
  /// PRIVATE (default) | PUBLIC. Only the creator flips it.
  visibility    String    @default("PRIVATE")
  /// SPDX id of the licence the source is published under (default MIT, creator-configurable).
  license       String    @default("MIT")
  latestBuildId String?
  latestVersion String?
  /// Generated page body (lib/cyrus-mods/doc.ts CyrusModDoc): summary, how to use,
  /// commands, permissions, config, versions + changelog, compatibility, files.
  doc           Json
  publishedAt   DateTime?
  /// Admin moderation: page hidden from everyone but its creator and admins.
  hiddenAt      DateTime?
  hiddenReason  String?
  /// Set when this mod started as a fork of another Cyrus mod.
  forkOfPageId  String?
  forkOfBuildId String?
  createdAt     DateTime  @default(now())
  updatedAt     DateTime  @updatedAt

  @@index([visibility, updatedAt])
  @@index([userId])
}

/// Community thread (parentId null) or comment (parentId = thread) on a Cyrus mod page.
model CyrusModPost {
  id           String    @id @default(cuid())
  pageId       String
  userId       String
  parentId     String?
  /// NOTE | BUG | FIX
  kind         String    @default("NOTE")
  /// OPEN | RESOLVED (threads; comments stay OPEN)
  status       String    @default("OPEN")
  /// The version (ModBuild id in the page's chain) this is about. Optional.
  buildId      String?
  title        String?
  body         String    @db.Text
  reportCount  Int       @default(0)
  hiddenAt     DateTime?
  hiddenById   String?
  hiddenReason String?
  resolvedAt   DateTime?
  resolvedById String?
  createdAt    DateTime  @default(now())
  updatedAt    DateTime  @updatedAt

  @@index([pageId, parentId, createdAt])
  @@index([userId, createdAt])
}

/// A viewer's report of a community post (one per viewer per post).
model CyrusModReport {
  id         String    @id @default(cuid())
  postId     String
  userId     String
  reason     String
  createdAt  DateTime  @default(now())
  resolvedAt DateTime?

  @@unique([postId, userId])
  @@index([resolvedAt, createdAt])
}

/// "Build on this mod": the forker's own copy of a published version. The
/// build service knows the SOURCE build id, so change requests on the copy are
/// sent with sourceBuildId as their base (app/api/mod-builder/builds).
model CyrusFork {
  /// The forker's ModBuild (status succeeded, jar copied).
  buildId       String   @id
  sourceBuildId String
  sourcePageId  String
  userId        String
  createdAt     DateTime @default(now())

  @@index([sourcePageId])
  @@index([userId])
}

/// "Notify me when it's back in stock" sign-ups for bare metal (lib/dedicated/stock-alerts.ts).
/// `kind` is the stock bucket ("gpu" today). One row per email+kind; re-signing up after a
/// notification clears `notifiedAt` so the next restock emails again. `userId` is set when a
/// signed-in customer signed up (attribution only, no relation so deleting a user keeps nothing tied).
model DedicatedStockAlert {
  id         String    @id @default(cuid())
  email      String
  kind       String
  userId     String?
  createdAt  DateTime  @default(now())
  notifiedAt DateTime?

  @@unique([email, kind])
  @@index([kind, notifiedAt])
}

content.thinking:
Given the scale of this existing system, I'm thinking my additions should be layered on top rather than invasive. I want a pure lifecycle module that derives a mod state (enabled, disabled, pending restart, failed, broken, outdated, installing, updating, etc.) from the server mod row, health verdict, and compatibility facts, along with a transition table governing how states move between each other.

I also want a compatibility checker comparing the mod's built-for version against the server's current version using GameSupport data, plus per-game log pattern detection for broken mods that extends the existing mod-health utilities with crash-loop detection. I'm planning an install-plan builder that derives packaging, restart, hot-reload, and warning steps from GameSupport.install, a creator-watch module that generates deduped, rate-limited warnings for creators based on published mod version ranges versus live server state, and an outdated-detection module. On the infrastructure side, I need a worker sweep that stays inert unless a settings flag enables it, with dry-run support, and I should check how settings are read via the existing getSetting utility. Finally, I'm noting that a crash loop after install should trigger auto-disable plus a notification.

For detecting crash loops specifically right after a Cyrus install, I'm considering a dedicated lifecycle worker that checks recent runtime crash/restart counts for newly installed mods and auto-disables them through the existing mod-op queue, gated behind the same settings flag. I also need to add a non-critical preference kind for mod health and creator notifications, checked against the existing prefs module, and build out server actions covering install planning, confirmed installs, enable/disable, update/updateAll, per-mod auto-update toggling, and creator warning listing/dismissal, including a deep link into the Cyrus dashboard with project and target version params. Now I'm moving into UI planning for how this surfaces in the mods tab.

For UI, I'm thinking through where lifecycle state badges and banners appear -- on installed library rows, server pages, and server list cards -- plus install dialogs for Cyrus and NxLabs, an extended update dialog with changelog support, and a creator warnings panel surfaced in both Cyrus/NxLabs and the portal. For data modeling, I'm leaning toward a dedicated CyrusCreatorWarning model with fields for dedupe keys, counts, timestamps, and email/dismiss tracking rather than overloading ModUpdateRun or Notification. I still need to confirm how the install engine handles automatic rollback on failed jobs, so I'm going to check the engine, queue, and mod-install action files to verify staged-write rollback behavior before finalizing this plan.

/**
 * Notification preferences: the stored shape, the pure helpers — and the POLICY
 * that decides which messages those preferences are allowed to suppress.
 *
 * Plain module (safe to import from server components; client components must
 * import TYPES ONLY — the `mayDeliverTo` helper below reaches for `./db`). The
 * `"use server"` action file may only export async functions, so all of this
 * lives here.
 *
 * WHY THIS FILE GREW A POLICY (2026-07-26)
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * `User.notificationPrefs` was written by the settings form and read by NOTHING
 * (QA-PRELAUNCH P1-32). A customer who unticked "Account email" still received
 * every receipt; the "Security alerts" toggle governed a channel that was never
 * built. That is the same defect this codebase keeps shipping: a control that
 * reports success and is read by nothing — the auto-suspend kill switch an
 * operator turned off before watching customer VMs get suspended anyway
 * (P1-5), and the domain-markup panel that displayed 0% while charging 25%
 * (P1-9).
 *
 * The dangerous half of fixing it is OVER-fixing it. If a preference could
 * suppress a declined payment, an imminent suspension, a security/2FA change or
 * a data-loss warning, then an unticked checkbox would silently swallow the one
 * message the customer had to see — and they would lose a server, or an
 * account, with no warning at all. That is strictly worse than the original bug.
 *
 * So suppressibility is decided by a message's TIER, declared once in the
 * catalogue below, and never by the call site. A send site cannot make itself
 * suppressible by passing the wrong flag, and an unrecognised kind resolves to
 * CRITICAL — if we guess wrong, we guess towards "delivered".
 */

export type NotificationPrefs = {
  /**
   * Non-urgent transactional EMAIL: payment receipts, activity notices.
   * Never covers the dunning sequence, suspensions or security changes.
   */
  email: boolean;
  /**
   * Product news / marketing. Unticking this also removes the address from the
   * campaign list (see `updateNotificationPrefs`) — the stored flag alone would
   * suppress nothing, because campaigns are addressed by email, not by user.
   */
  product: boolean;
  /**
   * Legacy key, pinned `true`.
   *
   * It used to render as a "Security alerts" toggle, which was dishonest twice
   * over: the channel it claimed to govern was never built (sign-in / token /
   * 2FA paths write audit rows only), and security, password and 2FA messages
   * must not be suppressible in the first place. Kept in the shape so
   * previously-stored values and the GDPR export keep round-tripping, and typed
   * as the literal `true` so no code path can ever write it back as
   * consent-withdrawn.
   */
  security: true;
};

export const DEFAULT_PREFS: NotificationPrefs = { email: true, product: true, security: true };

/**
 * Normalise whatever is stored in the Json column into a typed prefs object.
 * A missing or malformed key falls back to the default (opted IN) — the column
 * is nullable and predates this policy, so "absent" must never read as "the
 * customer opted out of everything".
 */
export function normalizePrefs(raw: unknown): NotificationPrefs {
  const p = (raw ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;
  return {
    email: typeof p.email === "boolean" ? p.email : DEFAULT_PREFS.email,
    product: typeof p.product === "boolean" ? p.product : DEFAULT_PREFS.product,
    security: true,
  };
}

The type-only exports should be fine since clients can import CreatorAlertView as a type from server.ts. Now I'm moving to the worker sweep logic in cyrus-lifecycle.ts, starting with the main sweep function gated by its setting.

Within the sweep, I need to handle two cases: processing health signals from recent ModUpdateRuns (creating BROKEN signals for failed verdicts, clearing them and notifying recovery for loaded verdicts, with owner notifications deduped per open signal), and detecting crash loops by checking recently-updated cyrus mods on running servers against their runtime/container state, pulling logs, and running judgeCrashLoop to decide whether to record a signal and potentially auto-disable the mod if safe and no job is already in flight.

After disabling a crashing mod, I realize the restart policy on the container should naturally pick up the fix on its next automatic restart since the jar is moved aside, so no explicit restart job is needed — just dedupe one CRASH_LOOP signal per server/mod/build. Then for auto-update, I check eligible cyrus mods with AUTO update mode, unpinned, no job in progress, head version differing from installed, compatibility and safety checks passing, and zero players online, enqueuing one update per server per sweep.

For the compat watch sweep, gated by its enable/dry-run flags, I need to gather all mod chains either publicly listed or installed via cyrus source, then for each chain pull builds, installs, and recent broken signals to build alert facts. I upsert alerts keyed by root build and alert key, resolve any that no longer apply, and send notifications respecting a weekly email cap per creator, with dry-run mode just logging without persisting.

I want to structure the core sweep as an exported function accepting injectable dependencies like a mail sender, so tests can run against a throwaway DB without actually emailing, and I'll reuse the existing mailer layout/button helpers for the alert email with a link back to the update page.

import { SPR, APP } from "@/lib/nx/sprites";
import { NX_ICONS, NX_ICON_TONE, type NxTone } from "@/lib/nx/icon-paths";

/* ── one dial for icon size, site-wide ────────────────────────────────────
   Every mark in the system is drawn a fixed multiple of the size its call site
   asks for. Applying it HERE rather than editing hundreds of call sites keeps
   the relative sizing intact: an icon that was deliberately smaller than its
   neighbour stays proportionally smaller, it is just bigger in absolute terms.
   Change this one number to retune the whole set.

   Note for anyone adding a primitive: scale exactly ONCE per rendered mark.
   `Plate` draws an `Icon` inside itself, so it scales its own BOX and passes
   the raw size through — scaling in both places would compound to 2.25x. */
export const ICON_SCALE = 1.5;
export const iconPx = (n: number) => Math.round(n * ICON_SCALE);

/**
 * One interface mark.
 *
 * VECTOR FIRST, sprite as the fallback. `lib/nx/icon-paths.ts` carries the set
 * redrawn as 24x24 paths; anything it defines renders as an inline SVG in
 * `currentColor`, and anything it doesn't — the sheet's brand row (linux,
 * docker, postgres…) and the five 3D product renders — still comes off
 * `public/nx/nxicons.webp` exactly as before.
 *
 * Why the switch is here rather than at 137 call sites: the sprite's marks are
 * pre-coloured, so one inside a tinted control renders in the SHEET's colour
 * instead of the control's (a teal shieldcheck on a violet "Admin" chip is the
 * bug that started this). Routing both through one component means every call
 * site gets `currentColor` without being edited, and a name with no vector yet

21239:## Mods tab declutter + Cyrus mods: engine installs, versions, NxLabs pages, community (2026-10-07, branch `feature/mods-tab-cyrus-mods`)
**Known limits.** Cyrus mods are skipped by the auto-updater (no upstream; they change only when the owner picks a version). Installing someone else's published Cyrus mod straight onto your server is not offered (download the jar, or Build on it to get your own copy) — owner decision.

**Verified in a sandbox harness (2026-10-07, throwaway DB `nxeon_agt_cyrusmods`, local mock of the build service serving REAL build records/jars/sources fetched from it earlier, the REAL `gameModSync` handler on a fake guest dir):** builds synced through `syncBuild` generated their pages; Cyrus install → engine → `state.json` + `ServerMod.versionId`; Versions dialog Update to latest (v1→v2, old jar backed up), Roll back (v2→v1), switch off/on (staged → one batch job), "Manage here" adoption of a pre-engine jar; publish; another preview account posted a bug on v1, the creator replied with a FIX and resolved it, the other account reported the reply (report row + count) and forked the mod (own private page "forked from"); source zip download (LICENSE + NXEON-CYRUS.md inside) and jar download; `/admin/cyrus-mods` launch switch on → outsider/anonymous get the published page (indexable) but still 404 on private pages, sitemap lists `/mods/cyrus` + the published page only; switch off → 404 + noindex again, nothing in the sitemap. NOT verified on a real game server (no customer servers touched; no throwaway VM provisioned).

Tests: `test/cyrus-mods.test.ts` (doc generation, slugs, licences, package versions, gate decisions + a source check that every route/action/download is gated, community rules, and the REAL engine path for a Cyrus jar against a fake guest: install → idempotent → update → disable → enable → rollback → refuse foreign version → uninstall, plus non-Paper and checksum refusals). Verification notes + screenshots: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-mods/`.

## Cyrus mod lifecycle: install, on/off, health, updates, creator warnings (2026-10-08, branch `feature/cyrus-v6-lifecycle`)

What happens to a Cyrus mod after it is built, on the customer's OWN servers. Everything goes through the existing mods engine (`lib/mods/engine.ts`: state file, backup, staged write, rollback) and the job queue (`lib/mods/queue.ts`, one `GAME_MOD_SYNC` per server under the per-server lock). Nothing here talks to a server directly from the portal.

**Code.** Pure rules (client-safe, unit-tested): `lib/cyrus/lifecycle/` (`support.ts` GameSupport registry + Cyrus game id ↔ server family; `compat.ts` version check + "outdated"; `state.ts` state machine; `install-plan.ts` the confirm step; `logs.ts` log patterns, broken/API-mismatch/crash-loop readers; `creator.ts` creator warnings + rate limit). DB half: `lib/cyrus/lifecycle/server.ts`. Actions: `lib/actions-cyrus-lifecycle.ts`. Worker: `worker/cyrus-lifecycle.ts` (sweeps `cyrus-lifecycle` 5 min, `cyrus-compat-watch` 6 h). Minecraft GameSupport: `lib/cyrus/games/minecraft.ts` (the other games' files come from the game agents; add one import line each to `lib/cyrus/lifecycle/support.ts` at merge).

**States** (`deriveLifecycle`; priority top to bottom):

```
                 install/update/enable/disable/remove queued
   ┌──────────────┐  (in flight: Installing · Updating · Enabling · Disabling · Removing)
   │  in flight   │──job failed (install)──────────────────────────────► FAILED ──retry──┐
   └──────┬───────┘──job failed (update: engine rolled back)──► ENABLED (note: kept vX)  │
          │ job ok, game loads mods at start                                              │
          ▼                                                                               │
   PENDING RESTART ──restart──► ENABLED ──game/loader moved past the mod / newer build──► OUTDATED
          │                       │  ▲                                                     │
          │      log error naming │  │ clean load after a fix                              │ update
          └──────────────────────►BROKEN ──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                  │ crash loop right after the change (evidence names it, or it's the only change)
                                  ▼
                          auto-disable ──► DISABLED ("We switched it off: …", config kept) ──enable──► …
```

**Install** (studio "Install to my server", NxLabs "Install on my server"): `installPlansFor(build, user)` builds one plan per server from GameSupport (`install.serverPath/packaging/needsRestart/hotReload/side`) + `checkCompat`: BLOCK on unsupported/too-old game versions, a newer version line, a stopped server, a non-Paper/Purpur server, a disabled/busy row, or a safety-blocked build; WARN (must be ticked) on legacy versions, unknown server version, built-for-older/newer in the same line, a server newer than anything Cyrus builds, safety notes, and "players must also install this" for client/both-side games. The same plan is re-checked server-side (`confirmPlan`) in `installCyrusMod` and the old `/api/mod-builder/builds/:id/install` route (409 + plan when a warning isn't acknowledged). Backup: the engine copies the replaced jar AND, new, the top-level files of the plugin's own folder (`plugins/<Name>/`, via `Resolution.alsoBackupDirs`) to `/root/.nxeon-mods/backups/<stamp>-<slug>/`; a failed write rolls back. Server game version = pinned `VERSION`, else the last version the log reported (mod-health now stores `plan.gameVersion`).

**Installing someone else's published mod** is coded but OFF: Setting `cyrus_install_published_enabled` (default "false", the 2026-10-07 owner decision). When on, only PUBLIC, not hidden, not safety-blocked versions, re-checked by the engine's jar source on every install/update (`lib/cyrus-mods/registry.ts loadCyrusJar`).

**Enable/disable**: the existing engine toggle (jar moved to `/root/.nxeon-mods/disabled/…`, config kept; `lib/mods/toggle-policy.ts` decides per game). `setCyrusModEnabled` for callers outside the Mods tab.

**Broken / outdated**: `worker/mod-health.ts` (inert unless `ENABLE_MOD_HEALTH=1`) now also runs `judgeCyrusLog` on Cyrus mods and stores `plan.cyrus` verdicts: runtime errors naming the plugin (`Could not pass event … to X`, `Task #n for X generated an exception`, `Error occurred while enabling X`) = Broken; `NoSuchMethodError`/`NoSuchFieldError`/`NoClassDefFoundError` on the Bukkit/Paper API/`UnsupportedClassVersionError` within 6 lines = Broken + "out of date for this version". The lifecycle sweep turns them into `CyrusModSignal` rows (BROKEN/RECOVERED) and tells the owner (in-app every time, email at most once per mod per server per day, kind `mod_health`, ACCOUNT tier). Crash loop: a Cyrus mod changed in the last 20 min, runtime crashed/restarting/not responding, ≥2 boots in the log since the change with no "Done (" after the last → auto-disable when the evidence names that mod or it was the only change, never for a disable that needs an acknowledgement; signals CRASH_LOOP + AUTO_DISABLED. Outdated: the server runs a version newer than the mod's newest build, or a newer version of the mod exists. Shown as: chip + note on the Mods tab row, a banner in the Mods tab, a banner on the server page (`CyrusServerBanner`), a chip on the game-server card (`/dashboard/games`).

**Updating**: the Versions dialog now lists "What changes" (every version between the installed one and the latest), keeps the rollback list, and has a per-mod "Update automatically" switch (`ServerMod.autoUpdate = AUTO`). "Update all" in the Updates view = ONE batch job with a target per mod. Auto-update (lifecycle sweep) only when nobody is online (player count known and 0), never to a version that already broke on that server, never across a compat BLOCK.

**Creator warnings** (Setting `cyrus_compat_watch_enabled`, default off; `cyrus_compat_watch_dry_run`, default on = record only): for every chain that is published or installed: NEW_GAME_VERSION (Cyrus can now build a newer version than the newest build), SERVERS_AHEAD (servers run it on a newer version; buildable or "Cyrus can't build for X yet"), ERROR_REPORTS (newest build broken on ≥2 servers in 7 days). One `CyrusCreatorAlert` per (mod, key); resolved automatically when it no longer applies; in-app once, email once and at most 2 per creator per week (kind `cyrus_creator_alert`, ACCOUNT tier, preference-gated). "Update with Cyrus for X" = `/dashboard/cyrus/<head>?retarget=X`: the studio opens the mod, prefills the change and sends `retarget: true` so `createModBuild` builds the change for X instead of the base's version (the build service already compiles each build against its own `mcVersion`). Shown on `/dashboard/nxlabs/cyrus` and the mod's own page (creator only), plus the bell. Admin switches + recent alerts (dry runs included): `/admin/cyrus-mods`.

**Fact worth knowing (2026-10-08):** Paper's own version list already has 26.1, 26.2 and 26.3; Cyrus builds 1.21.1–1.21.11 only. A server on 26.x shows Cyrus mods as Outdated ("Cyrus can't build for 26.x yet") and the creator warning has no build button until the build service gets 26.x classpaths.

**Schema (additive, end of schema.prisma):** `CyrusModSignal`, `CyrusCreatorAlert`. **Settings:** `cyrus_lifecycle_enabled`, `cyrus_compat_watch_enabled`, `cyrus_compat_watch_dry_run`, `cyrus_install_published_enabled`. **Notify kinds:** `mod_health`, `cyrus_creator_alert`.

**Tests:** `test/cyrus-lifecycle.test.ts` (pure: versions, compat, state machine + transition table, install plans incl. a client-side game, Paper log samples, crash loops, creator rules + rate limit). `test/cyrus-lifecycle-db.test.ts` (opt-in, node-2 throwaway DB + sandbox guest folder: install → pending restart → enabled → outdated → disable/enable → broken from a sample log → update with config backup → rollback → crash-loop auto-disable → auto-update gating → creator warning dry run / live / dedupe / resolve → 26.x servers ahead). Notes + screenshots: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-v6/lifecycle/`.
EOF

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

input.message:
**Lifecycle agent: report**

The Cyrus mod lifecycle is built and committed on `feature/cyrus-v6-lifecycle`, commit `89a9ea547e` (worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-v6-lifecycle`). It covers install with checks and a confirm step, on/off, Broken/Outdated warnings, updates and creator warnings. All tests pass on node-2: 35 pure and 9 end-to-end. Two things are not done because I wrapped up early as asked: the final `tsc` re-run, and the real-route screenshots. Nothing was deployed or merged, and no real server, production DB or email was touched.

**Tests**
- `test/cyrus-lifecycle.test.ts`: 35 of 35 pass. It covers version comparison, the compatibility check, the state machine, install plans (including a game where players also need the mod), sample Paper logs, crash loops and the creator-warning rate limit.
- `test/cyrus-lifecycle-db.test.ts`: 9 of 9 pass. It uses the throwaway node-2 database, a temp folder standing in for the server's disk, the real `GAME_MOD_SYNC` worker job and the real sweeps, with a fake mailer. It covers:
  - install → Pending restart → Enabled → Outdated;
  - disable keeps the mod on disk, enable puts it back;
  - a sample log line becomes Broken, and the owner is told once;
  - update keeps the config and backs it up with the old jar; rollback works;
  - a crash loop auto-disables the mod and notifies the owner;
  - auto-update waits while a player is online;
  - creator warnings: dry run records only, live run notifies and emails once, the warning resolves when the creator ships, and servers on 26.x are warned with no build button.
- The DB test writes a `server-only` stub into node-2's `node_modules`, the same trick `test/chat-agent-tools.test.ts` uses.
- `tsc` passed on an earlier snapshot only. Several later edits have not been typechecked (moving the alert helper, the setting for installing other creators' mods, the admin card, the creator-warning components, the DB test).

**What's built**
- **Rules** in `lib/cyrus/lifecycle/` (`support`, `compat`, `state`, `install-plan`, `logs`, `creator`), with the database side in `server.ts`.
- **`lib/cyrus/games/minecraft.ts`**: no game agent owned Minecraft, so I wrote its GameSupport file. `lifecycle/support.ts` has a one-line-per-game registry hook to fill at merge.
- **Install** from the studio and NxLabs uses one plan per server:
  - It blocks unsupported versions, the wrong server type, stopped servers and safety-blocked builds.
  - Warnings need a tick, and the server checks the ticks again, including in the old install API.
  - The engine now also backs up the plugin's config folder next to the old jar.
- **Mods tab**: a state chip and note on each Cyrus mod, a banner, a "What changes" list in the update dialog, a per-mod auto-update switch, and "Update all" as one job. There is also a banner on the server page and a chip on the game-server cards.
- **Worker** (`worker/cyrus-lifecycle.ts`): turns game-log errors into Broken warnings, auto-disables a mod that crash-loops the server right after its install, and applies opt-in auto-updates. It also raises the creator warnings.
- **"Update with Cyrus for X"** opens `/dashboard/cyrus/<id>?retarget=X`, which rebuilds the mod for that version.
- **Settings**, all inert by default: `cyrus_lifecycle_enabled` (off), `cyrus_compat_watch_enabled` (off), `cyrus_compat_watch_dry_run` (on). Admin switches are on `/admin/cyrus-mods`.
- **Additive schema**: models `CyrusModSignal` and `CyrusCreatorAlert`; notification kinds `mod_health` and `cyrus_creator_alert`, both email-optional.
- **Docs**: a new section, "Cyrus mod lifecycle", with the state diagram, in `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`.

**Finding:** Paper already ships Minecraft 26.1–26.3, but Cyrus only builds 1.21.1–1.21.11. Servers on 26.x will show Cyrus mods as Outdated, and creators get "Cyrus can't build for 26.x yet" with no build button.

**Decisions for the owner**
1. Installing another creator's published mod onto your own server: the 2026-10-07 docs record this as "not offered — owner decision". I built it but left it off behind `cyrus_install_published_enabled`. Turn it on or leave it?
2. When to switch on the lifecycle sweep and the creator warnings (leave dry run first). Broken detection also needs `ENABLE_MOD_HEALTH=1`, and auto-disable and auto-update need `ENABLE_REAL_GAMEMODS=1`.
3. Adding 26.x support to the build service.

**Left to do** (exact steps in `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-v6/lifecycle/PAUSED.md`)
- Re-run `tsc` under the lock.
- Take the screenshots: the harness (seed, creator-warning run, Playwright script) is ready in `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-v6/lifecycle/harness/`; it was never run.
- Run a schema push at merge.

The end-to-end test log is `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-v6/lifecycle/dbtest-e2e.log`. I deleted the harness copy from the worktree; it was never committed.
